ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a five-pointed star-shaped line diagram, with vertex D at the top, C on the left, E on the right, B at the lower left, and A at the lower right. At B, 58° is marked; this is the angle between lines BE and BD. At the intersection of lines BD and AC, 100° is marked. At the intersection of lines AD and BE, 93° is marked. What is required is the lower-right angle A, that is, the angle between lines AD and AC. Then reason: At the intersection of BD and AC, the given angle is 100°, and the needed adjacent angle is 180° - 100° = 80°. At the intersection of AD and BE, the given angle is 93°, and the needed adjacent angle is 180° - 93° = 87°. Starting from line BE, the turn angle to line BD is 58°; then from BD to AC, the turn angle is 80°, so the direction difference from BE to AC is 58° + 80° = 138°. And the direction difference from BE to AD is 87°. Therefore the angle between AD and AC at A is 138° - 87° = 51°.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: a five-pointed star has bottom-left tip B marked 58°, bottom-right tip A unknown, a 100° angle at the intersection of line BD with line AC, and a 93° angle at the intersection of line AD with line BE. Treat the relevant star edges as straight lines and compare their inclinations. The 100° crossing angle means the adjacent angle between BD and AC on the needed side is 180° - 100° = 80°. The 93° crossing angle means the adjacent angle between BE and AD on the needed side is 180° - 93° = 87°. Starting from line BE, turn 58° to line BD at B, then another 80° to line AC, so the direction difference from BE to AC is 58° + 80° = 138°. Since the direction difference from BE to AD is 87°, the angle between AD and AC at A is 138° - 87° = 51°.
